_readme: Optional per-unit absolute-time calibration. Each key under 'boards' is one physical board's factory-burned unique ID, exactly as reported in this project's serial handshake (visible in the console as '[INFO] board_program=... chip_id=...' when a board connects, or in a .dat file's header). 'ppm_offset' is how many parts-per-million the device's reported elapsed time exceeds true elapsed time, as measured by comparing the device's own reported duration against an independent time reference (e.g. an NTP-synchronized PC clock, over a long recording -- see README.md). Positive means the device's clock runs fast. plot.py applies corrected_time = raw_time / (1 + ppm_offset / 1e6) to any recording from a board listed here; boards with no entry are left uncorrected (this is the default -- calibration is opt-in, per unit, and this file starts empty). This is a per-unit measurement, not a general claim about the board type -- see README.md's timing-precision discussion for why. A single run's ppm_offset is noisy (see calibrate_timing.py's module docstring), so scripts/calibrate_timing.py accumulates repeated runs against the same board in 'runs' rather than overwriting; the top-level 'ppm_offset' it writes is the mean across 'runs' ('n_runs' of them), which is what plot.py actually reads -- run it several times (ideally at different times/room temperatures) rather than relying on a single run. Each run entry also records 'temp_c_start'/'temp_c_end' -- the board's own on-chip die temperature (Celsius) immediately before/after that run, queried only while idle so it never perturbs the recording's sampling cadence (null if unavailable, e.g. older firmware) -- so ppm_offset can be checked for a temperature correlation across runs directly, instead of only inferring it from varying the time of day.
